SummitConditions.Weather: In the clear under mostly clear skies

SummitOutlook.Discussion:
Surface high pressure over the region gradually shifts southward through the forecast period, with upper-level ridging moving overhead on Tuesday. A potent shortwave trough then approaches late Tuesday night.

Dry weather is expected through the forecast period under the influence of surface high pressure over New England. Other than a few upper-level clouds moving through from the north, mostly sunny skies prevail through Monday, with winds dropping to moderate speeds and remaining so into Tuesday night. The surface high slowly sags southward over the course of the day Monday into Monday night, with upper-level ridging beginning to shift overhead. This pattern will allow a warming trend to begin through mid week, with temperatures rising above seasonal averages on Tuesday. Upper and mid-level cloud coverage will increase Tuesday afternoon ahead of a shortwave trough embedded in the upper-level ridge rotating through the Great Lakes region towards New England, with skies becoming mostly cloudy overnight Tuesday. Though mostly cloudy above, the higher summits will remain in the clear however into Wednesday morning. As the axis of the ridge moves directly overhead late Tuesday night, winds will further decline, and may even become light and variable at times heading into early Wednesday morning.
Madelynn Smith -- Weather Observer and Meteorologist
Updated at 5:29 AM on Monday
